# THE CLOSED SPRINT GATES, one per line, in the order they closed.
#
# The build plan defines a gate as `phpunit --group sprint-N` green in CI, with every test
# in the group actually executed rather than skipped. This file is the list, and it is ONE
# file on purpose: ci.yml and release.yml both read it, so the two can no longer drift.
# They used to carry the list twice, and release.yml's copy had to be kept "in step" by
# hand - a comment is not a mechanism.
#
# A new sprint adds its group here on the day its gate closes, and the commit that adds it
# watches CI. A group listed here that no test carries makes the gate step RED (see
# bin/ci-group-counts.php), so a renamed or deleted group cannot pass unnoticed.
#
# sprint-3, sprint-4 and sprint-5 were added in Sprint 6; before that the loop silently
# stopped at sprint-2 and three gates were never asserted in CI at all. sprint-7 and
# sprint-8 were added in Sprint 8, for the same reason: both gates had closed and neither
# was asserted anywhere but on the machine that ran them. Each of the rest was added on the
# day its own gate closed.
#
# Notes that used to live in ci.yml's loop, kept because they are what a red group means:
#
#   sprint-9  is the first group whose subject depends on the DATABASE FLAVOUR: sql-select
#             spells its session statement timeout one way on MySQL and another on MariaDB,
#             and the wp-env container is the only MariaDB anyone on this project can reach.
#             A red sprint-9 in CI on a green local run is very likely that.
#   sprint-10 is the first group that is mostly about ORDERING and PAGING, so it is the
#             first a different COLLATION could move: list-posts compares titles in PHP
#             with strcasecmp when it merges its two queries, and the rows it merges arrived
#             in the server's own collation order.
#   sprint-11 is the first group whose expectations depend on the SITE'S TIMEZONE:
#             create-post's `date` stores post_date in local time and post_date_gmt in UTC,
#             and the tests compute the second from the first through get_gmt_from_date() on
#             the site rather than from a constant. Both Local sites and the container sit at
#             UTC, so the case that actually exercises the conversion sends an explicit
#             +05:30 offset.
#   sprint-seam is the first group whose subject is the plugin's own FILE LAYOUT: it proves
#             that a module registers through a checked door, that a module cannot publish a
#             write tool without declaring it one, and that the core assembles with no module
#             loaded at all. One of its tests runs a SUBPROCESS of PHP over a staged copy of the
#             plugin with modules/ deleted (tests/unit/BareCoreTest.php); it uses PHP_BINARY, so
#             it needs nothing on PATH, but a red sprint-seam on a green everything-else is
#             likely to be that test and not the seam.
#   sprint-14c is the first group that shells out to GIT: it builds a real `git archive` of
#             HEAD in a temp directory and reads the one file the plugin reads, which is the
#             only way to prove that a built zip carries its commit without installing one.
#             actions/checkout leaves a usable .git behind and the runner has git on PATH;
#             the test FAILS rather than skips if it does not.
